Quantum Espresso (QE, https://www.quantum-espresso.org/) is an open-source, plane-wave based, DFT software.

Here, QE is used to generate Density of State plots for Pr \( _{2} \) O \( _{3} \).

Convergence

Using a (8,8,8) k grid and a fixed ecutrho/ecutwfc=8 ratio, the ecutwfc was converged first.

The ecutwfc is converged at 120 Ry. A higher ecutrho/ecutwfc ratio did not change the energy.

The k_grid convergenced is benchmarked with Geometry Optimization of the unit cell.

from ase import Atoms
from ase.io.trajectory import Trajectory
from ase.eos import EquationOfState
from ase.io import read
from ase.units import kJ
from ase.filters import ExpCellFilter, FrechetCellFilter
from ase.optimize import LBFGS, QuasiNewton
from ase.calculators.espresso import Espresso, EspressoProfile


# Pseudopotentials from SSSP Efficiency v1.3.0
pseudopotentials = {'Pr': 'Pr.paw.pbe.z_13.atompaw.wentzcovitch.v1.0.legacy.upf', 'O': 'O.paw.pbe.z_6.ld1.psl.v0.1.upf'}

# Optionally create profile to override paths in ASE configuration:

    command='mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS /shared/apps/easybuild/x86_64/amd/zen4/software/QuantumESPRESSO/7.5-foss-2025b/bin/pw.x',
    pseudo_dir='/shared/home1/c.c22015584/Example-QuantumEspresso/mix-sssp-prec-pbe-lib-v2/library'
)

#Pr 90 720; O 50 600
#opt wfc 120 rho 960
wfc = 120
rho = 8 * wfc
input_data = {
    'system': {'ecutwfc': wfc, 'ecutrho': rho},
    #'disk_io': 'low',  # Automatically put into the 'control' section
    'tprnfor': True,
    'tstress': True,
    #'mixing_ndim': 25,
    'electron_maxstep': 150,

espresso = Espresso(profile=profile, pseudopotentials=pseudopotentials,
        kpts=(15,15,15),
        input_data=input_data)

Density of State with QE

Quantum Espresso (QE, https://www.quantum-espresso.org/) is an open-source, plane-wave based, DFT software.

Here, QE is used to generate Density of State plots for Pr \( _{2} \) O \( _{3} \).

Convergence

Using a (8,8,8) k grid and a fixed ecutrho/ecutwfc=8 ratio, the ecutwfc was converged first.

The ecutwfc is converged at 120 Ry. A higher ecutrho/ecutwfc ratio did not change the energy.

The k_grid convergenced is benchmarked with Geometry Optimization of the unit cell.

import numpy as np
from ase import Atoms
from ase.io.trajectory import Trajectory
from ase.eos import EquationOfState
from ase.io import read
from ase.units import kJ
from ase.filters import ExpCellFilter, FrechetCellFilter
from ase.optimize import LBFGS, QuasiNewton
from ase.calculators.espresso import Espresso, EspressoProfile


# Pseudopotentials from SSSP Efficiency v1.3.0
pseudopotentials = {'Pr': 'Pr.paw.pbe.z_13.atompaw.wentzcovitch.v1.0.legacy.upf', 'O': 'O.paw.pbe.z_6.ld1.psl.v0.1.upf'}

# Optionally create profile to override paths in ASE configuration:
profile = EspressoProfile(
    command='mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS /shared/apps/easybuild/x86_64/amd/zen4/software/QuantumESPRESSO/7.5-foss-2025b/bin/pw.x',
    pseudo_dir='/shared/home1/c.c22015584/Example-QuantumEspresso/mix-sssp-prec-pbe-lib-v2/library'
)

#Pr 90 720; O 50 600
#opt wfc 120 rho 960
wfc = 120
rho = 8 * wfc
input_data = {
    'system': {'ecutwfc': wfc, 'ecutrho': rho},
    #'disk_io': 'low',  # Automatically put into the 'control' section
    'tprnfor': True,
    'tstress': True,
    #'mixing_ndim': 25,
    'electron_maxstep': 150,
}


espresso = Espresso(profile=profile, pseudopotentials=pseudopotentials,
        kpts=(15,15,15),
        input_data=input_data)

oxide = read("EntryWithCollCode75481.cif")

cell = oxide.get_cell()
traj = Trajectory('oxide.traj', 'w')


with espresso.socketio(unixsocket='ase-espresso') as calc:

    oxide.calc = calc

    ecf = FrechetCellFilter(oxide, constant_volume=True)
    qn = QuasiNewton(ecf)
    traj_opt = Trajectory('opt_x.traj', 'a', oxide)
    qn.attach(traj_opt)

    qn.run(fmax=0.01)
    energy = oxide.get_potential_energy()

    traj.write(oxide)

Density of State with QE

Quantum Espresso (QE, https://www.quantum-espresso.org/) is an open-source, plane-wave based, DFT software.

Here, QE is used to generate Density of State plots for Pr \( _{2} \) O \( _{3} \).

Convergence

Using a (8,8,8) k grid and a fixed ecutrho/ecutwfc=8 ratio, the ecutwfc was converged first.

The ecutwfc is converged at 120 Ry. A higher ecutrho/ecutwfc ratio did not change the energy.

The k_grid convergenced is benchmarked with Geometry Optimization of the unit cell.

import numpy as np
from ase import Atoms
from ase.io.trajectory import Trajectory
from ase.eos import EquationOfState
from ase.io import read
from ase.units import kJ
from ase.filters import ExpCellFilter, FrechetCellFilter

from ase.calculators.espresso import Espresso, EspressoProfile

    command='mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS /shared/apps/easybuild/x86_64/amd/zen4/software/QuantumESPRESSO/7.5-foss-2025b/bin/pw.x',
    pseudo_dir='/shared/home1/c.c22015584/Example-QuantumEspresso/mix-sssp-prec-pbe-lib-v2/library'
)

#Pr 90 720; O 50 600

wfc = 120

input_data = {

    'tprnfor': True,

    'electron_maxstep': 150,
}


espresso = Espresso(profile=profile, pseudopotentials=pseudopotentials,

traj = Trajectory('oxide.traj', 'w')

ab inito molecular dynamics with CP2K

CP2K is an open-source souce software that supports both DFT and classical force fields. Its DFT functionality is based on the mixed Gaussian and plane waves approaches GPW and GAPW.

Here, an ab inito molecular dynamics simulation of a water box is performed with CP2K.

Convergence

With a big-enough REL_CUTOFF=60, converge the CUTOFF parameter first for a water molecule.

Too large CUTOFF values lead to poor grid distribution, the convergence region is in the middle (CUTOFF=400 is chosen).

Then the REL_CUTOFF is converged.

Density of State with QE

Quantum Espresso (QE, https://www.quantum-espresso.org/) is an open-source, plane-wave based, DFT software.

Here, QE is used to generate Density of State plots for Pr \( _{2} \) O \( _{3} \).

Convergence

Using a (8,8,8) k grid and a fixed ecutrho/ecutwfc=8 ratio, the ecutwfc was converged first.

The ecutwfc is converged at 120 Ry. A higher ecutrho/ecutwfc ratio did not change the energy.

The k_grid convergenced is benchmarked with Geometry Optimization of the unit cell.

import numpy as np
from ase import Atoms
from ase.io.trajectory import Trajectory
from ase.eos import EquationOfState
from ase.io import read
from ase.units import kJ
from ase.filters import ExpCellFilter, FrechetCellFilter
from ase.optimize import LBFGS, QuasiNewton
from ase.calculators.espresso import Espresso, EspressoProfile


# Pseudopotentials from SSSP Efficiency v1.3.0
pseudopotentials = {'Pr': 'Pr.paw.pbe.z_13.atompaw.wentzcovitch.v1.0.legacy.upf', 'O': 'O.paw.pbe.z_6.ld1.psl.v0.1.upf'}

# Optionally create profile to override paths in ASE configuration:
profile = EspressoProfile(
    command='mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS /shared/apps/easybuild/x86_64/amd/zen4/software/QuantumESPRESSO/7.5-foss-2025b/bin/pw.x',
    pseudo_dir='/shared/home1/c.c22015584/Example-QuantumEspresso/mix-sssp-prec-pbe-lib-v2/library'
)

#Pr 90 720; O 50 600
#opt wfc 120 rho 960
wfc = 120
rho = 8 * wfc
input_data = {
    'system': {'ecutwfc': wfc, 'ecutrho': rho},
    #'disk_io': 'low',  # Automatically put into the 'control' section
    'tprnfor': True,
    'tstress': True,
    #'mixing_ndim': 25,
    'electron_maxstep': 150,
}


espresso = Espresso(profile=profile, pseudopotentials=pseudopotentials,
        kpts=(15,15,15),
        input_data=input_data)

oxide = read("EntryWithCollCode75481.cif")

cell = oxide.get_cell()
traj = Trajectory('oxide.traj', 'w')


with espresso.socketio(unixsocket='ase-espresso') as calc:

    oxide.calc = calc

    ecf = FrechetCellFilter(oxide, constant_volume=True)
    qn = QuasiNewton(ecf)
    traj_opt = Trajectory('opt_x.traj', 'a', oxide)
    qn.attach(traj_opt)

    qn.run(fmax=0.01)
    energy = oxide.get_potential_energy()

    traj.write(oxide)

ab inito molecular dynamics with CP2K

CP2K is an open-source souce software that supports both DFT and classical force fields. Its DFT functionality is based on the mixed Gaussian and plane waves approaches GPW and GAPW.

Here, an ab inito molecular dynamics simulation of a water box is performed with CP2K.

Convergence

With a big-enough REL_CUTOFF=60, converge the CUTOFF parameter first for a water molecule.

Too large CUTOFF values lead to poor grid distribution, the convergence region is in the middle (CUTOFF=400 is chosen).

Then the REL_CUTOFF convergence is investigated, and 60 is found to be a reasonable value.

Pre-equilibration with MACE

The water box with 27 H2O was prepared with ASE and equilibrated with a mace-mp foundation model.

import numpy as np

import ase.units as units
from ase import Atoms
from ase.build import molecule
#from ase.calculators.tip3p import TIP3P, angleHOH, rOH
from ase.constraints import FixBondLengths
from ase.io.trajectory import Trajectory
from ase.md import Langevin
from ase.optimize import LBFGS
from mace.calculators import mace_mp


# Set up water box at 20 deg C density
atoms = molecule("H2O")

vol = ((18.01528 / 6.022140857e23) / (0.9982 / 1e24)) ** (1 / 3.0)
atoms.set_cell((vol, vol, vol))
atoms.center()

atoms = atoms.repeat((3, 3, 3))
atoms.set_pbc(True)

calc = mace_mp(model="medium", dispersion=False, default_dtype="float32", device='cpu')

atoms.calc = calc

opt = LBFGS(atoms)

opt.run(fmax=0.05)


tag = 'mace_27mol_equil'


md = Langevin(
    atoms,
    timestep=1 * units.fs,
    temperature=300 * units.kB,
    friction=0.01,
    logfile=tag + '.log',
)

traj = Trajectory(tag + '.traj', 'w', atoms)
md.attach(traj.write, interval=1)
md.run(4000)

ab inito molecular dynamics with CP2K

CP2K is an open-source souce software that supports both DFT and classical force fields. Its DFT functionality is based on the mixed Gaussian and plane waves approaches GPW and GAPW.

Here, an ab inito molecular dynamics simulation of a water box is performed with CP2K.

Convergence

With a big-enough REL_CUTOFF=60, converge the CUTOFF parameter first for a water molecule.

Too large CUTOFF values lead to poor grid distribution, the convergence region is in the middle (CUTOFF=400 is chosen).

Then the REL_CUTOFF convergence is investigated, and 60 is found to be a reasonable value.

Pre-equilibration with MACE

The water box with 27 molecules was prepared with ASE and equilibrated with a mace-mp foundation model.

import numpy as np

import ase.units as units
from ase import Atoms
from ase.build import molecule
#from ase.calculators.tip3p import TIP3P, angleHOH, rOH
from ase.constraints import FixBondLengths
from ase.io.trajectory import Trajectory
from ase.md import Langevin
from ase.optimize import LBFGS
from mace.calculators import mace_mp


# Set up water box at 20 deg C density
atoms = molecule("H2O")

vol = ((18.01528 / 6.022140857e23) / (0.9982 / 1e24)) ** (1 / 3.0)
atoms.set_cell((vol, vol, vol))
atoms.center()

atoms = atoms.repeat((3, 3, 3))
atoms.set_pbc(True)

calc = mace_mp(model="medium", dispersion=False, default_dtype="float32", device='cpu')

atoms.calc = calc

opt = LBFGS(atoms)

opt.run(fmax=0.05)


tag = 'mace_27mol_equil'


md = Langevin(
    atoms,
    timestep=1 * units.fs,
    temperature=300 * units.kB,
    friction=0.01,
    logfile=tag + '.log',
)

traj = Trajectory(tag + '.traj', 'w', atoms)
md.attach(traj.write, interval=1)
md.run(4000)

####k grid

The k grid sampling is converged in terms of energy from (2,2,2).

A well converged k grid of (4,4,4) is chosen without incurring much additional cost.

AIMD simulation

Here is an input file generated with ASE based on the MACE pre-equilibrated geometry.

!!! Generated by ASE !!!
&FORCE_EVAL
   METHOD Quickstep
   STRESS_TENSOR ANALYTICAL
   &DFT
      BASIS_SET_FILE_NAME BASIS_MOLOPT
      POTENTIAL_FILE_NAME POTENTIAL
      &KPOINTS
         SCHEME MONKHORST-PACK 4 4 4
      &END KPOINTS
      &MGRID
         NGRIDS 4
         REL_CUTOFF 60
         CUTOFF [eV] 5.442277204873448682e+03
      &END MGRID
      &SCF
         MAX_SCF 50
         &PRINT
            &RESTART OFF
            &END RESTART
         &END PRINT
      &END SCF
      &PRINT
         &E_DENSITY_CUBE OFF
         &END E_DENSITY_CUBE
         &MO_CUBES
            NLUMO 4
            NHOMO 4
            WRITE_CUBE .FALSE.
            &EACH
               MD 30
            &END EACH
         &END MO_CUBES
      &END PRINT
      &LS_SCF
         MAX_SCF 50
      &END LS_SCF
      &XC
         &XC_FUNCTIONAL
            &PBE
            &END PBE
         &END XC_FUNCTIONAL
      &END XC
   &END DFT
   &PRINT
      &STRESS_TENSOR ON
      &END STRESS_TENSOR
   &END PRINT
   &SUBSYS
      &COORD
         O 1.278915707442245697e+00 2.194621646636388146e+00 2.574272241630262581e+00
         H 1.164263954964662728e+00 2.755036642588189810e+00 3.373923015847648088e+00

Density of State with QE

Quantum Espresso (QE, https://www.quantum-espresso.org/) is an open-source, plane-wave based, DFT software.

Here, QE is used to generate Density of State plots for Pr \( _{2} \) O \( _{3} \).

Convergence

Using a (8,8,8) k grid and a fixed ecutrho/ecutwfc=8 ratio, the ecutwfc was converged first.

The ecutwfc is converged at 120 Ry. A higher ecutrho/ecutwfc ratio did not change the energy.

The k_grid convergenced is benchmarked with Geometry Optimization of the unit cell.

import numpy as np
from ase import Atoms
from ase.io.trajectory import Trajectory
from ase.eos import EquationOfState
from ase.io import read
from ase.units import kJ
from ase.filters import ExpCellFilter, FrechetCellFilter
from ase.optimize import LBFGS, QuasiNewton
from ase.calculators.espresso import Espresso, EspressoProfile


# Pseudopotentials from SSSP Efficiency v1.3.0
pseudopotentials = {'Pr': 'Pr.paw.pbe.z_13.atompaw.wentzcovitch.v1.0.legacy.upf', 'O': 'O.paw.pbe.z_6.ld1.psl.v0.1.upf'}

# Optionally create profile to override paths in ASE configuration:
profile = EspressoProfile(
    command='mpirun -np $SLURM_NTASKS /shared/apps/easybuild/x86_64/amd/zen4/software/QuantumESPRESSO/7.5-foss-2025b/bin/pw.x',
    pseudo_dir='/shared/home1/c.c22015584/Example-QuantumEspresso/mix-sssp-prec-pbe-lib-v2/library'
)

#Pr 90 720; O 50 600
#opt wfc 120 rho 960
wfc = 120
rho = 8 * wfc
input_data = {
    'system': {'ecutwfc': wfc, 'ecutrho': rho},
    #'disk_io': 'low',  # Automatically put into the 'control' section
    'tprnfor': True,
    'tstress': True,
    #'mixing_ndim': 25,
    'electron_maxstep': 150,
}


espresso = Espresso(profile=profile, pseudopotentials=pseudopotentials,
        kpts=(15,15,15),
        input_data=input_data)

oxide = read("EntryWithCollCode75481.cif")

cell = oxide.get_cell()
traj = Trajectory('oxide.traj', 'w')


with espresso.socketio(unixsocket='ase-espresso') as calc:

    oxide.calc = calc

    ecf = FrechetCellFilter(oxide, constant_volume=True)
    qn = QuasiNewton(ecf)
    traj_opt = Trajectory('opt_x.traj', 'a', oxide)
    qn.attach(traj_opt)

    qn.run(fmax=0.01)
    energy = oxide.get_potential_energy()

    traj.write(oxide)
